title: Cartesian pushout products preserve right-anodyne maps
statement: Use simplicial sets, horns and degreewise products as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Call a map right anodyne if it belongs to the smallest class containing all isomorphisms and the horn inclusions $\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ for $m\geq1$ and $0<j\leq m$, and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Let $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ be right anodyne and let $k:K\hookrightarrow L$ be any monomorphism of small simplicial sets. The canonical pushout-product map $$ (A\times L)\amalg_{A\times K}(B\times K)\longrightarrow B\times L $$ is right anodyne. Here a monomorphism of simplicial sets means a degreewise injective map, and a pushout means the colimit of the indicated span [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A transfinite composite means $Z_0\to Z_\theta$ for a small ordinal-indexed diagram $(Z_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ with $Z_\beta$ the colimit of the earlier stages at every nonzero limit $\beta\leq\theta$. A map $f:U\to V$ is a retract of $g:U'\to V'$ if there are maps $a:U\to U'$, $b:V\to V'$, $r:U'\to U$, $s:V'\to V$ with $ga=bf$, $fr=sg$, $ra=1_U$, and $sb=1_V$.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 4.2.5.3, right-anodyne assertion (not the unrelated Stacks tag 0153). Online source read; not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Write $\theta_{i,k}$ for the stated map. Identify a monomorphism with its image inclusion. Degreewise its domain is the union $(A\times L)\cup(B\times K)$ inside $B\times L$, since the intersection is $A\times K$. This union is a pushout: compatible maps out of the two subsets agree exactly on the intersection. Operators preserve all three subsets, so the same universal map is simplicial. Thus $\theta_{i,k}$ is a monomorphism. Commutative squares in either input induce maps on products and on this pushout, respecting identities and composition. In particular section and retraction squares in either input give section and retraction squares of the corresponding $\theta$-maps.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, degreewise details of the pushout-product construction and its functoriality.

proof.text: The class $W$ of right-anodyne maps is weakly saturated by [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], with exactly the nonzero-index horn convention in the item. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-saturation] to this $W$. For each fixed monomorphism $k$, the monomorphisms $i$ with $\theta_{i,k}$ right anodyne form a weakly saturated class; the same holds in the other variable with $i$ fixed. Consequently it is enough in the first variable to check the generating right horns, and it is enough in the second variable to check boundary inclusions once all monomorphisms are expressed by boundary attachments as below.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof: weak saturation of T and T-prime.

proof.text: Put $e:\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $b_m:\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, where the boundary is the union of proper faces and $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. By Step 1, $\theta_{e,b_m}$ is $X_0\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times\Delta^m$ from [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary]. Each successor $X_q\hookrightarrow X_{q+1}$ is a pushout of $\Lambda_{q+1}^{m+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{m+1}$. Because $1\leq q+1\leq m+1$, every attaching horn is a right horn. Pushout and finite-composition closure therefore make $\theta_{e,b_m}$ right anodyne. At $m=0$ there is one attachment, $\Lambda_1^1=\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$; this includes the zero-dimensional boundary case omitted in the source's last paragraph.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), finite horn filtration, including m=0.

proof.text: Let $h:U\hookrightarrow V$ be any small simplicial monomorphism. The existing relative skeletal filtration [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] presents it as a countable composite of pushouts of coproducts of the maps $b_m$. To handle a coproduct indexed by a small set $S$, well-order $S$ and at stage $\alpha$ take the coproduct of full simplices at indices $<\alpha$ and boundaries at indices $\geq\alpha$. A successor map is a pushout of one $b_m$, and a limit is the union of earlier stages; the empty coproduct is an identity. Thus the class in Step 2 with first variable $e$ contains each coproduct, each skeletal attachment and the final composite. It follows that $\theta_{e,h}$ is right anodyne for every $h$. All indexing sets and their well-order types are small.

source.place: Proposition 1.5.5.14 (0077), proof of (b): relative skeleton and well-ordered serialization of coproducts; applied to T-prime in Proposition 4.2.5.3.

proof.text: For a generating right horn $f:\Lambda_a^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$ and $0<a\leq n$, put $P=(\Delta^1\times\Lambda_a^n)\cup(\{1\}\times\Delta^n)$ and $g=\theta_{e,f}:P\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$. The section of arrows $f\to g$ inserts the vertex $0$ in both source and target. Define the retraction on vertices by $r(0,t)=t$ and $r(1,t)=\max(a,t)$. It is monotone on each level, and across levels $t\leq u$ implies $r(0,t)=t\leq\max(a,u)=r(1,u)$. For an $s$-simplex given by increasing maps $\epsilon:[s]\to[1]$ and $t:[s]\to[n]$, its image is the increasing map $j\mapsto r(\epsilon(j),t(j))$; this formula commutes with precomposition by every simplicial operator. Thus it defines a simplicial map, and $r(0,t)=t$ proves the retraction identities on both source and target. A simplex in $\Delta^1\times\Lambda_a^n$ omits in its second coordinate some vertex $v\ne a$; applying $r$ can only add $a$, so still omits $v$. On $\{1\}\times\Delta^n$ the image has vertices at least $a>0$, so omits $0\ne a$. Hence $r(P)\subseteq\Lambda_a^n$, which proves both commutative squares and makes $f$ an arrow retract of $g$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.10 (00TG), explicit monotone retraction; its horn-preservation check is written out here.

proof.text:
Fix an arbitrary monomorphism $k:K\hookrightarrow L$ and the horn $f$ of Step 5. Functoriality in Step 1 makes $\theta_{f,k}$ a retract of $\theta_{g,k}$. Set $h=\theta_{f,k}$; it is a monomorphism by Step 1. Both $\theta_{g,k}$ and $\theta_{e,h}$ identify, after the coordinate associator, with the inclusion into $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\times L$ of the same union
$$ (\{1\}\times\Delta^n\times L)\cup(\Delta^1\times\Lambda_a^n\times L)\cup(\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\times K). $$
Indeed distributing the two domains degreewise gives precisely these three subsets, with the redundant subset $\{1\}\times\Delta^n\times K$ already included. Their operators and inclusion maps coincide. Step 4 makes $\theta_{e,h}$ right anodyne. Isomorphism and retract closure therefore make $\theta_{f,k}$ right anodyne.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof: reduction of g to the endpoint inclusion; the triple-union identification is explicit.

proof.text: For each fixed $k$, Step 6 puts all generating right horns in the weakly saturated class of Step 2. That class contains isomorphisms as well, hence contains the smallest class generated from these horns and isomorphisms under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. This is exactly the right-anodyne class [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Thus $\theta_{i,k}$ is right anodyne for every right-anodyne monomorphism $i$ and every simplicial monomorphism $k$, with precisely the map in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, completion of the weak-saturation reduction.
